definitions.gloss: onsen egg; egg slow-cooked at a low temperature
definitions.explanation: An egg cooked slowly in hot water around 65–70°C so that the yolk stays creamy while the white turns soft and custard-like. Originally made using hot-spring water.

examples.japanese: {温泉|おんせん}{卵|たまご}を{作|つく}る。
{丼|どんぶり}の{上|うえ}に{温泉|おんせん}{卵|たまご}をのせる。
examples.english: Place an onsen egg on top of the rice bowl.

examples.japanese: {温泉|おんせん}{卵|たまご}は{白身|しろみ}がやわらかく、{黄身|きみ}がとろりとしているのが{特徴|とくちょう}だ。
examples.english: An onsen egg is characterized by its soft white and runny yolk.

notes:
Compound of {温泉|おんせん} (hot spring) + {卵|たまご} (egg); the name comes from originally cooking eggs in hot-spring water. Often shortened to {温玉|おんたま} in casual speech and on menus.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {温泉|おんせん}{卵|たまご}をのせる: to top (a dish) with an onsen egg
- {温泉|おんせん}{卵|たまご}を{作|つく}る: to make an onsen egg

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {半熟|はんじゅく}{卵|たまご}: soft-boiled egg — boiled briefly so the white sets firm but the yolk stays runny; an onsen egg instead has a soft, custard-like white
